snapshot.description: Stand barefoot or in flat shoes. Find the three foot tripod points. Shift weight forward/backward and side-to-side while keeping all three points connected and the toes relaxed.

definition.description: Stand on a clean dry level surface with both heels, first metatarsal heads, fifth metatarsal heads, and relaxed toes in contact. Shift pressure forward, return to center, backward, return to center, left, return to center, then right and return to the same centered bilateral stance without stepping. Keep the contacts connected while pressure changes, keep toes relaxed, and use the selected hands-free or light wall-touch support. One full four-direction circuit is one repetition.

definition.description: With one target foot supported on a clean dry level surface, press the hallux gently into the floor to the prescribed comfortable submaximal effort. Keep the heel and first and fifth metatarsal heads down, keep lesser toes relaxed, hold while breathing, then reduce pressure with control until the hallux returns to the same supported start. Record left and right repetitions and hold seconds separately. Standing hands-free, standing light wall-touch, and seated stable-bench support are exact variants.

definition.description: Stand with both heels, first metatarsal heads, fifth metatarsal heads, and relaxed long toes supported on a clean dry level surface. Gently shorten both feet by drawing the metatarsal heads toward the heels without curling or lifting the toes. Keep forefoot contacts while rising directly upward into a comfortable bilateral calf raise, lower both heels with control to the same flat-foot start, then fully relax the arch set before the next repetition. The heels intentionally leave contact during the rise; first and fifth metatarsal head contact and quiet toe behavior remain required. Hands-free and light wall-touch are exact variants.

legacy.description: Create a gentle bilateral arch without curling the toes, rise into a slow calf raise while forefoot contacts stay organized, lower both heels with control, then fully relax the arch before the next repetition.
legacy.tempo: gentle arch set, slow rise, controlled lower, and full arch release
legacy.loadNote: Track exact hands-free or wall-touch variant, valid repetitions, arch set, toe behavior, forefoot contacts, heel path, range, first fault, symptoms, rest, duration, station reset, and overlapping foot, calf, Achilles, balance, running, landing, jumping, agility, and lower-body exposure.
legacy.cardSummary: A bilateral ordered arch-set-to-calf-raise-to-lower-to-release cycle with explicit heel and forefoot contact rules.
legacy.coachLanguage: Verify exact support, bilateral arch set, quiet toes, forefoot contact during intentional heel rise, controlled lower, full release, symptoms, dose, and downstream foot and calf budget. Do not force range or treat this as a clinical protocol.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Make a small arch without clawing the toes. Rise straight up, lower slowly, then relax the arch before the next rep.

setup: both feet flat and toes long
execution_steps: rise directly up with organized forefeet

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is a safe visible foot-contact station, exact selected support, comfortable bilateral arch-set and heel-rise range, sequence comprehension, symptoms, communication, planned dose, and downstream foot and calf demand; never participant classification.
readinessChecks: Confirm exact hands-free or wall-touch bilateral variant and clear visible station.
Confirm toes and forefeet can stay organized through a small controlled heel rise and lower.
Confirm arch set, rise, lower, release, stop signal, and exit.
Review cumulative foot, calf, Achilles, balance, and lower-body exposure.
stopSigns: Sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, or post-trauma pain or participant stop request.
Instability, painful pinching, persistent cramp, numbness, tingling, weakness, circulation, skin, or control change.
Toe curl, forefoot contact loss, uncontrolled heel path, or missing release that cannot be restored after reduced range or more support.
Unsafe surface, hygiene, wall, visibility, space, traffic, communication, or exit.
contraindications: Current symptoms, restriction, skin, circulation, neurologic concern, or loading tolerance conflicts with exact arch set or heel raise.
No safe visible compliant station or selected support.
The intended service is diagnosis, treatment, Achilles rehabilitation protocol, maximal testing, single-leg, step, loaded, rebound, or another identity.
commonSubstitutions: Use wall-touch only after support, difficulty, logistics, duration, and budgets are recomputed.
Use Short-Foot Drill or Standing Calf Raise only when the removed or changed action fits and all checks are rerun.
Do not assume single-leg, step, seated, bent-knee, loaded, sustained-hold, rebound, resisted, or clinical forms are equivalent.
